sn7.8:3.1: For him, the “three knowledges” would have been the Vedas.
sn7.8:3.4: An oblation of milk-rice may be offered to various deities, and is commonly associated with fertility rites. It should be offered to brahmins (eg. Khādira Gṛhyasūtra 4.3; Pāraskara Gṛhyasūtra 3.9.8; Gobhila Gṛhyasūtra 3.8, 4.6.13; Śāṅkhāyana Gṛhyasūtra 3.11.16, 4.16.5), but only those who study the Vedas (Gautama Dharmasūtra 1.5.30). It should not be cooked for one’s own consumption (Manu 5.7). It counteracts inauspicious dreams (Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka 11.4). Manu 3.271 says such an offering is efficacious for a year. Compare [snp3.4](), where rice cake is offered instead. | _Somaṁ_ is _so imaṁ_, not a reference to _soma_.
sn7.8:5.1: This verse sets out the Buddha”s “three knowledges”: recollection of past lives, clairvoyance of rebirth, and ending of rebirth.
sn7.8:8.1: See [sn2.9:7.3]() and note. Also note that, while _gāthā_ is sometimes said to exclude Rig Vedic verse, this does not mean it excludes Brahmanical verse altogether (see eg.Atharva Veda 10.10.20, 15.6.4, 20.103.1; Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.17.9). Rather, it was a later or more secular style.
sn7.8:8.4: “Since there is such a principle” is _dhamme sati_, “there being the law of nature”.
